verticalInfoCards.note: Devotees are allowed to touch the main lingam (Sparsha Darshan), which is a unique feature.

verticalInfoCards.description: The temple complex is vast and also houses the Bhramaramba Devi temple, making it a rare site of dual spiritual importance.

overview.title: Overview
overview.text: Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple, located atop the Nallamala Hills in Srisailam, is a unique and highly revered shrine. It is one of the few places in India that is revered as both a Jyotirlinga and a Shakti Peeth, celebrating Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati together.

mythology.title: Mythological Origin
mythology.text: As per legend, Lord Kartikeya, upset after losing a race to his brother Ganesha, went to the Kroncha hills. A distraught Shiva and Parvati followed him and resided on the Srisailam peak to be near him. Shiva appeared as Arjuna on a day of full moon (Mallika Pushpa), hence the name Mallikarjuna.

architecture.title: Architectural Highlights
points: The temple is a classic example of Dravidian architecture with high stone walls and towering gopurams.
The main sanctum is ancient, with the lingam believed to be self-manifested (Swayambhu).
The temple complex is fortified with massive prakarams (walls) built during the Vijayanagara Empire.
Intricate carvings on pillars and walls depict stories from the Puranas and epics.
The Bhramaramba temple within the complex is where Sati's neck is believed to have fallen.

significance.title: Spiritual Significance
points: It is the only place in India that is both a Jyotirlinga and a Shakti Peeth.
Adi Shankaracharya is said to have composed his famous 'Sivananda Lahari' hymn here.
The darshan of the lingam is believed to be equivalent to the darshan of Kailash.
The presiding deities are referred to as Mallikarjuna Swamy and Bhramaramba Devi.

events.event: Mentioned in ancient texts like the Mahabharata and Skanda Purana.
Evidence of worship and patronage by the Satavahana dynasty.
Major renovations and additions by the Vijayanagara kings, including Krishnadevaraya.

items.text: Sparsha Darshan (touching the lingam) is believed to absolve one of all sins.
Goddess Parvati took the form of a bee (Bhramara) to slay a demon, hence she is known as Bhramaramba.
A holy dip in the Pathala Ganga (Krishna River) is a customary ritual before visiting the temple.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Srisailam Mallikarjuna offers a rare and powerful pilgrimage experience, where the divine masculine and feminine energies converge. It is a journey into ancient history, mythology, and profound spirituality amidst the serene Nallamala forests.

aboutPostCards.title: Major Festivals
items: Maha Shivratri Brahmotsavam – A grand 11-day festival.
Ugadi – Telugu New Year celebrated with special rituals.
Dasara – Celebrated with grandeur at the Bhramaramba temple.

aboutPostCards.title: Nearby Attractions
items: Pathala Ganga – The sacred spot in the backwaters of the Krishna River.
Srisailam Dam – One of the largest dams in India offering breathtaking views.
Akka Mahadevi Caves – Natural caves accessible by boat.
Srisailam Tiger Reserve – A large tiger reserve in the Nallamala forest.

methods.title: By Road
methods.description: Srisailam is well-connected by bus services from major cities in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, like Hyderabad and Vijayawada.

methods.title: By Helicopter
methods.description: Chartered helicopter services can be arranged but are not common for regular travel.

methods.title: Nearest Railway
methods.description: Markapur Road Railway Station (85 km) and Kurnool City (180 km).

methods.title: Nearest Airport
methods.description: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (HYD), is approximately 215 km away.
